analyst_view.overall: Early view: A meeting of two promoted sides with the lowest-scoring league games in the division: Schalke's nine matches have produced 16 goals and Paderborn's 19. Paderborn are unbeaten in four under Ralf Kettemann and well organised, while Schalke have scored all their league goals away from home but may be without Robin Gosens and possibly goalkeeper Loris Karius after their collision at Hoffenheim.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.6 goals, which is very low. I lean slightly higher: Schalke's attack works better on the road (all five league goals away, and expected goals above 2.5 at Hoffenheim), and Paderborn scored twice at home against Frankfurt last time. A goalless draw is possible, but two goals feels more like the middle.

corners.text: The site expects 10.4 corners, 6.1 for Paderborn. Both sides have used back threes with wing-backs, which produces crosses, and nothing in the news points away from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.4 cards, which looks low for a game near the bottom. Paderborn took three yellows at Gladbach and Kettemann was booked against Frankfurt, and Schalke have collected two in each of their last two games. I lean higher.

shots.text: The site has 28.6 shots. Neither side has a high-volume attack, and Paderborn's 0-0 at Gladbach was a typical low-volume game for them, so I lean slightly lower on volume while expecting the few chances to be decent ones.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 on target. Paderborn keep opponents to few clear chances (11 conceded in nine) and Schalke's attack is unsettled, so I lean slightly lower.
